text:
An undrafted defenseman who worked his way up from Bowling Green and the AHL, Sean Walker now has a Stanley Cup ring from Carolina's 2025-26 run. This season he has 12 points (4 goals) in 23 games at about 21 minutes a night.

Some of that is luck. He is shooting 8.5%, above his usual range for a defenseman, and the Hurricanes have scored 6.55 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. His own chances are modest (2.35 expected goals, the quality of chances, on 47 shots).

The underlying play is strong, though it comes inside a strong team. Carolina takes 58% of the five-on-five expected goals with Walker on, slightly below what it does without him. Evolving-Hockey valued him at 1.3 wins last season, mostly from even-strength defense (86th percentile at limiting chances against, after adjusting for strong teammates). That defensive work is the real reason he plays these minutes. We'd treat the points as a bonus and watch whether his ice time, down about a minute and a half over his last ten, holds.
